slide_text: Quick Check: A brand-new user signs up and hasn t rated any movies. What happens when we try to recommend movies? A. The system recommends the most popular movies B. The similarity vector is all zeros no direction, no meaningful recommendations C. It crashes with a division error D. It works fine using the defaults

fragments.text: Answer: B. With no ratings, the user s vector is all NaN (filled to mean). Their direction is meaningless. This is the cold-start problem the system can t help until it knows your taste.

slide_text: Quick Check: Netflix has ~300 million users and ~20,000 titles. Which approach produces a smaller similarity matrix? A. User-user (300M 300M) B. Item-item (20K 20K) C. Both are the same size D. Neither is feasible

fragments.text: Answer: B. A 20K 20K matrix has 400 million entries. A 300M 300M matrix has 90 quadrillion . At scale, item-item collaborative filtering is far more practical.
